clue.text: All in Paris look for custom

definitions.meaning: the French word for 'all', as spoken in Paris
to solicit business pushily, as a street seller does

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition asks for French: 'all' in French is the same four letters as the English word for hustling for trade.
explanation.definitionFit: French for 'all' is tout, and a tout is someone who pesters passers-by to buy, so both senses share the spelling.

clue.text: Switch which may be built into trains

indicators.note: letters assembled or constructed into a new shape, so the following words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A railway switch, the points that might be installed in a rail network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'built' rearranges the ten letters of INTO and TRAINS together; 'which may be' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A switch is a change from one state to another, which is a shift or changeover.

clue.text: American woman pilot

parts.note: her is a pronoun standing for a woman

explanation.surface: An American aviator who happens to be female.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pilot' looks like an aviator noun but works as a verb: to guide someone to their seat.
explanation.definitionFit: To pilot someone is to guide or escort them, which is what an attendant at a theatre or wedding does.

clue.text: Work-place antagonism

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a work of music
a position is a place or location

explanation.surface: Hostility between colleagues in the office.
explanation.definitionFit: Antagonism is hostility or resistance, the stance taken by a rival side.

clue.text: Quietly shelves certain promises

parts.note: P, for piano, is the musical direction meaning quietly
ledges are narrow shelves, as on a cliff or window

explanation.surface: Someone discreetly sets aside particular promises, as politicians do.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm promises are vows or solemn undertakings, such as those made to a charity.

clue.text: The appearance of food not raised under glass?

definitions.text: The appearance of food not raised under glass?

parts.words: The appearance of food not raised under glass?
parts.note: reads as vegetables grown outdoors rather than in a greenhouse; really an exposure of bedrock breaking through the soil

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as OUT CROP and it is produce grown in the open air; as one word it is rock that 'appears' at the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Geologically, rock that shows above the ground surface is said to appear, and the question mark flags the split reading as produce grown outdoors.

clue.text: One wise man's got the picture!

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a mage is a magus, one of the wise men

explanation.surface: One of the Magi has grasped the idea at last.
explanation.walkthrough: ''s got' is only a link joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture is a likeness or representation, as in a painted portrait.

clue.text: Sick jokes occasioning bad feeling

parts.note: ill means sick
humour is jokes taken collectively

explanation.surface: Tasteless jokes cause resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sick jokes' reads as one phrase about black comedy, but the words split: ILL plus HUMOUR; 'occasioning' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad feeling is resentment or bad temper, a sour mood.

clue.text: No Greek character is other than superior

parts.note: taken as written
nu is the thirteenth letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Missing a Greek letter makes a thing lowly.
explanation.walkthrough: U and non-U were 1950s British labels for upper-class and not-upper-class speech and manners; 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The label marks speech or manners as lacking upper-class polish, i.e. not posh.

clue.text: Toasting a writer

definitions.meaning: making bread go golden under heat
Robert or Elizabeth Barrett, Victorian poets

explanation.walkthrough: 'Toasting' suggests raising a glass, but here it is cooking bread until it colours.
explanation.definitionFit: Toast is bread cooked until it goes golden, and Robert and Elizabeth Barrett were married Victorian poets of that surname.

clue.text: Bear north for a change, though far from agreeable

indicators.note: suggests something altered, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, spelt out in full

explanation.surface: Turning a bear towards the north, though it is very unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' rearranges BEAR and NORTH together; 'though' links. 'north' is used in full, not as N.
explanation.definitionFit: Something detestable or repugnant is very far from pleasant.

clue.text: Weary of everything stylish

parts.note: all means everything
in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'

explanation.surface: Tired of anything fashionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Being exhausted, completely spent, is the idiomatic British sense of the phrase.

clue.text: Pay the little twister!

definitions.meaning: a small threaded fastener turned into wood

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pay the little twister!' reads as settling up with a crook; it is slang for wages plus a small fastener.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses the word for a wage, and a small threaded fastener is driven home by twisting.

clue.text: Descriptive of Cheddar's scenery?

parts.note: Cheddar Gorge is a limestone ravine in Somerset, so its landscape is full of ravines; the question mark admits the pun

explanation.walkthrough: Cheddar suggests cheese, but Cheddar Gorge is a dramatic limestone canyon in Somerset, England; split the answer as 'gorge-ous'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stunning or beautiful, and punningly 'full of ravines', which suits the Somerset canyon.

clue.text: Order given when the ratings collapsed

indicators.note: something that has fallen apart, so the letters of these words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written; ratings are ordinary sailors

explanation.surface: A command issued when the sailors fell in a heap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapsed' rearranges THE RATINGS; 'given when' links. 'Order' is a verb: to put in order, tidy up.
explanation.definitionFit: To order things is to tidy or arrange them neatly, putting them right.

clue.text: Records incredible stories with just one left out

indicators.note: out means excluded, so the letter for left is removed

parts.note: tall, as in a tall story, means hard to believe
lies are untrue stories

explanation.surface: Someone writes down unbelievable tales, leaving out only one.
explanation.walkthrough: TALL and LIES together have two Ls; 'just one left out' drops one L.
explanation.definitionFit: Records as a verb means keeps a count or score, as on a scorecard.

clue.text: Refuse to go in here

parts.note: reads as declining to enter; really 'refuse' is rubbish, and this is where rubbish goes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' wants to be the verb (decline), but it is the noun meaning rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A receptacle where rubbish is put in a public place is exactly where refuse goes.

clue.text: Look glum, having swallowed dope, and keel over

indicators.note: one thing taking another inside it, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: to pout is to push the lips out sulkily
an ass is a fool, as is a dope

explanation.surface: Someone sulks after taking drugs, then collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' suggests drugs but means a fool here.
explanation.definitionFit: To keel over is to faint or collapse, losing consciousness.

clue.text: Little effort is needed to deal with this post!

definitions.text: Little effort is needed to deal with this post!

parts.words: Little effort is needed to deal with this post!
parts.note: reads as light mail to sort; really a job that demands hardly any work

explanation.walkthrough: 'post' suggests letters to answer, but means a job: one with pay and no real duties.
explanation.definitionFit: A cushy job, paid but carrying almost no duties, needs little effort.

clue.text: Go on, act stupidly — ruin the figure!

indicators.note: acting foolishly and wrecking things, so the letters of the preceding words are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Encouragement to behave foolishly and spoil one's physique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupidly' and 'ruin' both signal rearranging GO ON and ACT.
explanation.definitionFit: An eight-sided polygon is a geometric figure.

clue.text: Love without object

parts.note: no means without, as in 'no money'
a thing is an object

explanation.surface: Love with no particular target.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis, love is a score of zero.
explanation.definitionFit: Love is the tennis score of zero, which means none at all.

clue.text: An underground toiler set against a goddess

parts.note: a miner works underground
V, for versus, means against

explanation.surface: A coal miner pitted against a deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman deity of wisdom, counterpart of Athena, is a goddess.

clue.text: A dragon of a medico -— awfully stern

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor

indicators.note: suggests something mangled, so the word after it is rearranged

explanation.surface: A forbidding doctor, very strict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges STERN to NSTER; 'of a' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragon is a mythical beast, and a fierce, frightening person, a fearsome creature.

clue.text: One laying about a boat-crew to effect some improvement

indicators.note: surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a hen is a bird that lays eggs
an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: Someone sitting round a rowing team to make things better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One laying' suggests a person lying down, but means an egg-laying bird; 'to' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To intensify or raise something is to make it greater, an improvement.

clue.text: A has-been in distress may ring one repeatedly

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'A has-been in distress may ring one repeatedly' (5) for GONER. 'A has-been' defines it, but no parse of the rest builds GONER without leaving 'may' and 'repeatedly' unused or using 'in' twice; no source found.
annotationWithheld.clue: A has-been in distress may ring one repeatedly

clue.text: Hold accommodating many fish

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, i.e. many
ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A ship's hold packed with plenty of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold' looks like a ship's hold, but it is a verb: to grip; 'accommodating' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To grip tightly or hang on is to clasp.

clue.text: It can contain the prison uprising that's pointless

indicators.note: one thing holds another inside it, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means read backwards

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure or prison

explanation.surface: A jail riot that achieves nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' turns PEN to NEP, which 'can contain' puts inside IT; 'that's' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Pointless here means clumsy and lacking skill, without a point.

clue.text: A cut must be properly organised

explanation.walkthrough: 'must be' only joins the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A light haircut is the noun, and neat and orderly is the adjective sense.

clue.text: A small bird needs endless dressing

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: robing is putting on clothes

explanation.surface: A tiny bird needs a bandage applied without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs' links.
explanation.definitionFit: The red-breasted songbird is a small garden bird.

clue.text: To cross Crete isn't unusual

indicators.note: something not normal, so the letters of the words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written; the apostrophe is no letter

explanation.surface: Sailing across to the Greek island is quite common.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges the letters of CRETE ISNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines that cross meet and pass over each other at a point.

clue.text: A person to draw — or a plant

parts.note: a man is a person
to drag is to pull or draw
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone to sketch, or a plant to grow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draw' suggests sketching but means pull.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandrake is a Mediterranean plant whose root was used as a narcotic.

clue.text: Senseless' comeback causing shock

indicators.note: coming back means returning the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: nuts means crazy, out of one's senses

explanation.surface: A mad person's reply that causes alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'causing' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To shock or daze someone leaves them stupefied.
